reason: Copying the nuclear DNA addresses the genome goal before the cell divides.
expectation: The nucleotides will be used to replicate the genome, though the result may show an intermediate stage.

alternatives.reason: Building the spindle also supports division, but I chose genome copying first.

effect: The genome is copied, and the sister chromatids still need separation, so building the spindle is a useful next step.
reaction: The distinction between copying all nuclear DNA and making proteins is helpful.
reason: The centrosomes, tubulin and motors should form the machinery needed to separate chromosomes.
expectation: I expect a spindle to form between the centrosomes, though chromosome attachment may come later.

alternatives.reason: Growing the cell is also a goal, but I want to prepare for chromosome separation first.

effect: The spindle is built, but chromosomes have not yet been separated; the daughter-cell goal is now visible.
reaction: The overlapping fibres make the construction clear, though the spindle has not acted yet.
reason: Combining the copied genome with the spindle should advance chromosome separation.
expectation: I expect the spindle to attach to and separate the sister chromatids, possibly as an intermediate toward two cells.

alternatives.reason: Cell growth remains a goal, but I want to follow the newly built spindle first.

effect: The chromosome sets are separated, but the cell still shares one cytoplasm; cell growth remains unfinished.
reaction: The distinction between chromosome separation and division into two cells is clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should help grow the cell's surface and contents.
expectation: I expect the phospholipids and proteins to contribute to cell growth, possibly as an intermediate before division.

effect: The phospholipids and proteins formed membrane vesicles, an intermediate that can now be added to the cell.
reaction: The vesicles make the membrane-growth route clearer.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should advance cell growth.
expectation: I expect the vesicles to contribute membrane to the growing cell, though other growth may still be needed.

effect: The cell body has grown, completing the growth goal; it can now be combined with the separated chromosome sets.
reaction: The added cytoplasm and organelles make clear that growth involves more than expanding the membrane.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should bring the growth and chromosome-separation results together.
expectation: I expect a cell prepared for division, though separating its cytoplasm may require another step.

effect: Two daughter nuclei have formed, but the cytoplasm remains shared; the cell still needs to divide.
reaction: The separate nuclei make the remaining division step clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination; actin and myosin should help divide the cell.
expectation: I expect actin and myosin to constrict the cell and separate it into two daughter cells.

effect: Actin and myosin completed the division, producing two separate pluripotent daughter cells and completing the chapter.
reaction: The final picture brings the earlier genome and cell-growth paths together; the note about different gene-expression patterns invites curiosity.

mostWorthwhile.text: Separating the copied chromosomes was most worthwhile: the picture and explanation distinguish distributing sister chromatids from actually dividing the cytoplasm.

leastWorthwhile.text: The vesicle and cell-growth sequence was somewhat repetitive, with only one combination offered at each decision, though it clarified that growth involves more than membrane expansion.

surprise.text: The genome-copying result emphasized that noncoding DNA is copied too, unlike the production of a particular protein.

arbitrary.text: Combining phospholipids with new proteins to make vesicles felt somewhat indirect until the result showed how they could contribute to membrane growth. The offered compatibility guided the choice.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the final connection between shared genomes and different gene-expression patterns suggests an interesting next topic. Some specialist terms, such as pluripotent and centrosomes, could use clearer definitions for the intended audience.
